lines: Vince has bought lunch three years running and finished Week 11 in last place again. The steakhouse has penciled in a four-peat.
Vince's lunch tab so far: three years, six seafood towers, and enough Caymus to count as a Napa investor.
Kevin and JD have never bought lunch. Every glass of Caymus they've ever had was on someone else.
Art is vegetarian. The league goes to a steakhouse most years anyway. Art's order: the sides, the bread and the Caymus list.
Most years, Art's vegetarian option at lunch is watching everyone else eat two seafood towers.
Two seafood towers isn't an appetizer. It's a message about who's paying.
Caymus pairs well with steak, shellfish and someone else's credit card.
Somewhere in Napa, the Caymus people check the Sunday Tables standings every Monday.
The winner picks the restaurant. History says it will be a steakhouse. Sorry, Art.
JD leads the season with four Team pots, and has never bought lunch. Some people are born lucky; JD was born with someone else's Caymus.
JD has been the week's biggest winner four times: Weeks 2, 6, 8 and 11. The restaurant reservation is practically in JD's name.
Galli has four Team pots (one shared), level with JD for the most, and is still −$584. The Lightning table has cost Galli $854. The Team table giveth; the Lightning table taketh, with interest.
Kevin and Galli have each had eight picks score nothing this season, the most in the league; for Galli, five of those didn't even play. Kevin's latest: Jalon Daniels in Week 11, for −$48.
JohnO is +$479 in Lightning and −$220 in the Team table. Brilliant at the side bets, allergic to the main event.
Mxue has gone up, down, up, down for all eleven weeks. Week 11 was up. Week 12 has been warned.
Week 10: six of seven Team tables had Kenneth Walker III, who didn't play. JD had Chuba Hubbard instead, alone: 29 points and the pot.
Week 2: Puka Nacua didn't play, and Art, Mxue, Galli and JohnO had all picked Puka. One DNP, four victims.
Same Team table, three times: Art and Galli lost to Vince in Week 2, Mxue and Galli split the Week 7 pot, Art and Mxue lost to JD in Week 10. Copying homework works one time in three.
Jahmyr Gibbs has been on Art's Team table in ten of eleven weeks, and on Mxue's and Vince's in nine. Original thinking is not this league's strength.
Galli has picked Bijan Robinson in nine of eleven weeks. That's not a pick, that's a marriage.
Kevin has had Christian McCaffrey on the Team table in ten of eleven weeks, and Ja'Marr Chase in nine. Kevin doesn't pick a team, Kevin renews it.
Week 8: Art's Tee Higgins took $266 off the rest of WR2, and Art's Lamar Jackson scored 0. Art giveth, Art taketh away.
Drake Maye scored 3 for Vince in Week 10 and cost $62 in QB2. Galli had the same Drake Maye in Week 5 and couldn't stop scoring. Same quarterback, different owner, different universe.
Vince has the season's two lowest Team tables: 43 in Week 6, then 52 in Week 7. Back to back. Commitment.
Vince won the Week 2 Team pot with 114, then gave $56 back in Lightning and finished the week +$64. Even Vince's best week came with a refund.
Art was up in each of the first four weeks, then down in five of the next seven. The hot start is now −$50.
Kevin has been the week's biggest winner three times and the week's biggest loser three times. Kevin doesn't do quiet Sundays.
Galli has won four Team pots (one shared) and been the week's biggest loser three times. Galli contains multitudes.
Art and JohnO have tied for the top of a Lightning column three times. Great minds, identical points.
Vince has finished a week up only four times in eleven. Lunch for seven doesn't pay for itself.
JD has made 16 Team-table picks this season that nobody else made, the most in the league. The consensus rankings are more of a suggestion.
Week 4: JD was the only one on Kenneth Walker III. Walker scored 29 and JD took the Team pot. The experts were not consulted.
JD's Team-table method: open the consensus rankings, then pick someone else.
Mxue's draft picks arrive eventually. The league has learned to bring snacks.
The Lightning draft has no pick clock. Mxue is the reason someone keeps suggesting one.
Lineups lock at the first kickoff, good or bad. Galli knows why.
Every league has a rule named after someone. Ours locks the lineups at kickoff. Thanks, Galli.
Mxue keeps the scores, writes up the rules and runs the site, and is somehow in the money. The league would like an audit.
Every number on this site was checked by Mxue. Every Mxue pick was not.
Only two of Mxue's Team-table picks this season were ones nobody else made, the fewest in the league. The scorekeeper plays it by the book.
The site warns when a player is on all seven Team tables. It has no warning for Mxue turning in the same Team table as Art. Week 10 suggests it needs one.
Mxue has lost more close Lightning columns than anyone. The scorekeeper re-checked the math. It's still a loss.
If the ticker ever stops moving, don't panic. Mxue is probably still making a pick.
Mxue maintains this site for free. The league pays in complaints and the occasional seafood tower.
Mxue: scorekeeper, rulebook editor, site builder, and still not first. Some jobs don't come with perks.
